newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-O'Reilly says NZ paper staying near home.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-O'Reilly says NZ paper staying near home.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Plc chairman Tony O'Reilly said on Friday he had no plans to expand distribution of the freshly acquired New Zealand Herald beyond its base on the country's north island.
"There will be changes. They will be evolutionary, not revolutionary," O'Reilly said in a telephone interview.
As to distributing the Herald throughout the country, he said, "The market in New Zealand is essentially the northern island."
Independent this year bought a controlling 85 percent stake in Wilson & Horton, publisher of the Herald, in a deal valuing the leading New Zealand newspaper company at NZ$1.32 billion.
The Irish company will eventually buy the outstanding 15 percent, he said. He declined to set a timetable for the purchases.

O'Reilly also declined to detail the company's plans for the Herald but he said, typically, Independent seeks to increase the cover price of a new newspaper property and increase coverage of art, sports and other areas.
